title: Anaphylaxis (Severe Allergic Reaction)
summary: A severe allergic reaction can kill within minutes. Use an adrenaline (epinephrine) auto-injector immediately and call for help.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for any suspected anaphylaxis
when: Breathing difficulty, wheeze, hoarse voice or throat tightness
Swelling of the tongue, lips or throat
Pale, floppy, dizzy, faint or collapse
After any use of an adrenaline auto-injector

steps.title: Use the adrenaline auto-injector now
steps.text: If they have one, help them use it, or give it yourself, into the outer thigh (through clothing if needed). Follow the instructions on the device.

steps.title: Position
steps.text: Lay them flat. If breathing is difficult, let them sit up. If they are pregnant, lay them on their left side. Do not let them stand or walk, even if they feel better.
steps.caution: Sudden standing up can cause collapse.

steps.title: Second dose
steps.text: If symptoms do not improve after 5 minutes and another auto-injector is available, give a second dose.

steps.title: Monitor and be ready for CPR
steps.text: Stay with them. If they become unresponsive and are not breathing normally, start CPR.

doNot: Do not wait to see whether symptoms get worse before giving adrenaline
Do not let them stand or walk
Do not rely on antihistamines to treat anaphylaxis
